description: Baseline soak. Waiting out the window in which a compromised or broken release gets yanked is a supply-chain control, not just stability hygiene. Security updates are exempt: vulnerabilityAlerts defaults to minimumReleaseAge=null and prCreation=immediate.
Majors soak twice as long; they carry the most behavioural risk.

High-trust upstreams soak for 3 days rather than a week. The bar is a publisher with a published security process and staged rollout, whose patch releases are themselves frequently the security fix -- for those, a full week delays the fix more than it guards against a bad release. The Go toolchain is the only member today; both the mise pin and the go.mod directive are covered so the grouped PR below cannot half-unblock. Majors are excluded and keep the 2-week tier.

Renovate defaults minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour to timestamp-required, which holds an update forever when its datasource publishes no release timestamp, rather than soaking it. Observed here for go:golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck, which a dry run reported as having no releaseTimestamp. Relaxed only here: gomod keeps the strict default because those modules link into the shipped binary and the Go module proxy always supplies a timestamp, so there is no starvation risk to trade against.
GitHub Actions are CI plumbing, so scope them ci(actions). Digest pinning stops a moved tag from changing what executes in a release-signing workflow.
mise.toml pins the toolchain shared by local dev and CI, so scope it ci(mise).
Go modules link into the npc binary, so scope them deps(go).

Automerge non-major action updates; CI gates the merge, so a bad bump fails its own PR rather than landing on main. Deliberately excludes the digest updateType: a digest that moves under an unchanged tag is the exact substitution pinDigests exists to catch, so it gets a human.

Automerge non-major lint, hook, and scanner tooling. None of it ships in the binary, and `mise run check` gates the PR. Enumerated rather than negated so that adding a tool to mise.toml forces a deliberate decision about whether it may automerge.
Release tooling stays manual. A goreleaser or ko regression corrupts published artifacts at tag time, which is downstream of every CI gate that would otherwise catch it.
Runtime dependencies stay manual. npc is a cryptographic tool and these are the modules linked into what users execute.

GOTOOLCHAIN=local makes the mise pin the toolchain outright, so the go.mod directive and mise.toml must move together or the build fails on a version mismatch. One grouped PR keeps them consistent and reviewable.
Last rule wins: no major update automerges, whatever the per-manager grants above allow.
